Publication forest figure of estimated effects

Source: R/margot_plot_effects.R
margot_plot_effects.Rd

Draws estimated effects and their confidence intervals as a horizontal forest figure built to a journal column width: a label column, one interval panel per contrast, optional decimal-aligned numeric columns, and a footer with one axis title and a key. Every dimension is derived from the content and the target width, so the same call works across studies with different numbers of outcomes, label lengths, contrasts and scales.

Usage

margot_plot_effects(
  data,
  xlab,
  plot = c("estimate", "raw"),
  columns = character(),
  column_titles = list(),
  family_title = NULL,
  group_titles = NULL,
  order = c("estimate", "given"),
  contrast_titles = NULL,
  key_labels = NULL,
  width_mm = 120,
  size_pt = 6.5,
  label_max_mm = 45,
  stripe = TRUE,
  digits = NULL,
  margin_mm = 1,
  family = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Tidy effects table, usually from margot_lmtp_effects(). Required columns: outcome, estimate, lower, upper and conf_level. Optional columns: label, contrast, type ("difference", the default, or "ratio"), group, raw_estimate, raw_lower, raw_upper (differences in original units), mean_reference, mean_intervention, evalue and evalue_bound. Tables from other estimators can be supplied in the same format.

xlab

Axis title for the interval panels. A line break in the string starts a second line.

plot

Plotted quantity: "estimate" or "raw" (the original-unit columns).

columns

Numeric columns to the right of the panels, in order: any of "plotted" (the plotted quantity), "estimate", "raw", "means" (reference and intervention means) and "evalue" (point and interval E-values).

column_titles

List with one c(title, subtitle) per column; NULL entries use the defaults. "{ci}" is replaced by the interval label (for example "99.58% CI"), and a subtitle written "a|b" puts one sub-heading over each number.

family_title

Title above the label column, for example "Outcome".

group_titles

Named character vector mapping values of group to display titles, in display order.

order

"estimate" (descending within each group, by the first contrast's plotted estimate) or "given" (row order of data).

contrast_titles

Named character vector of titles for the contrasts, used when there is more than one.

key_labels

Labels for the filled and open points. Default "Interval excludes 0" and "Interval includes 0" (1 for ratios); NULL omits the key.

width_mm

Final figure width in millimetres, margin included. Nature uses 89, 120 and 183 mm; Science and PNAS use similar column widths.

size_pt

Type size in points at print size.

label_max_mm

Widest label column before labels wrap.

stripe

Shade alternate rows.

digits

Decimals for the estimate and original-unit columns; NULL chooses them as described above.

margin_mm

White margin inside width_mm.

family

Font family; NULL chooses as described above.

Value

A patchwork object. Attributes: size_mm (final width and height), margin_mm, layout_mm (widths of the label column, each interval panel and each numeric column), axis (breaks, data range, limits and smallest gap between tick labels in mm), font (family, font file and its MD5 checksum) and plotted (the drawn estimate and interval for each outcome and contrast, top to bottom, with excludes_null, which sets the filled point). Save it with margot_save_effects_plot(), which uses size_mm.

Details

Points are estimates and horizontal lines are the intervals in data. A filled point marks an interval that excludes the null (0 for differences, 1 for ratios) and an open point one that includes it, so status does not depend on colour. Ratios are drawn on a log axis. The axis breaks bracket every interval and the null, are chosen so that adjacent tick labels stay at least 2.5 mm apart at the stated width, and the call stops rather than draw a figure that would cut off part of an interval.

Numbers in the columns are rounded for display only. The number of decimals is the fewest, from two, at which no limit of an interval that excludes the null prints as the null itself; digits overrides it. Each character is placed from its unkerned advance width, so decimal points align exactly down each column, and the text stays live in the PDF.

Type is set at size_pt (default 6.5 pt) in Arial when it is installed, falling back to Helvetica, Liberation Sans or DejaVu Sans with a warning. Text widths, and so the layout, depend on the font file, which is recorded on the returned object.

See also

margot_lmtp_effects(), margot_save_effects_plot()

Examples

effects <- data.frame(
  outcome = c("y_warmth", "y_trust", "y_belonging"),
  label = c("Warmth", "Trust in others", "Sense of belonging"),
  estimate = c(0.12, -0.03, 0.05),
  lower = c(0.07, -0.08, -0.01),
  upper = c(0.17, 0.02, 0.11),
  conf_level = 1 - 0.05 / 3
)
fig <- margot_plot_effects(effects, xlab = "Difference in mean outcome, SD units",
  columns = "estimate", family_title = "Outcome", width_mm = 120)
attr(fig, "size_mm")
#>     width    height 
#> 120.00000  28.96041
